title: Refuse and Recyclable Material Collectors
description: Collect and dump refuse or recyclable materials from containers into truck. May drive truck.

tasks.text: Dump refuse or recyclable materials at disposal sites.
Dismount garbage trucks to collect garbage and remount trucks to ride to the next collection point.
Clean trucks or compactor bodies after routes have been completed.
Make special pickups of recyclable materials, such as food scraps, used oil, discarded computers, or other electronic items.
Operate automated or semi-automated hoisting devices that raise refuse bins and dump contents into openings in truck bodies.
Operate equipment that compresses collected refuse.
Inspect trucks prior to beginning routes to ensure safe operating condition.

clusters.label: Operating Vehicles, Mechanized Devices, or Equipment

tasks.text: Drive trucks, following established routes, through residential streets or alleys or through business or industrial areas.
Refuel trucks or add other fluids, such as oil or brake fluid.

clusters.label: Communicating with Supervisors, Peers, or Subordinates

tasks.text: Communicate with dispatchers concerning delays, unsafe sites, accidents, equipment breakdowns, or other maintenance problems.
Check road or weather conditions to determine how routes will be affected.
Tag garbage or recycling containers to inform customers of problems, such as excess garbage or inclusion of items that are not permitted.

skills.name: Operations Monitoring
skills.def: Watching gauges, dials, or other indicators to make sure a machine is working properly.

skills.name: Operation and Control
skills.def: Controlling operations of equipment or systems.

skills.name: Active Listening
skills.def: Giving full attention to what other people are saying, taking time to understand the points being made, asking questions as appropriate, and not interrupting at inappropriate times.

skills.name: Speaking
skills.def: Talking to others to convey information effectively.

skills.name: Critical Thinking
skills.def: Using logic and reasoning to identify the strengths and weaknesses of alternative solutions, conclusions, or approaches to problems.

skills.name: Equipment Maintenance
skills.def: Performing routine maintenance on equipment and determining when and what kind of maintenance is needed.

skills.name: Reading Comprehension
skills.def: Understanding written sentences and paragraphs in work-related documents.

skills.name: Coordination
skills.def: Adjusting actions in relation to others' actions.

skills.name: Data base user interface and query software
skills.def: Software to query, present, or edit information stored in a database sytem. Examples: Dossier software, Mileage logging software.

skills.name: Analytical or scientific software
skills.def: Software to capture data, perform analysis, or generate reports or visualizations to support scientific research. Examples: AMCS Platform.

skills.name: Facilities management software
skills.def: Software to track, monitor, or analyze a facility's assets, space availability, or tenant information. Examples: Computerized maintenance management system CMMS.

skills.name: Materials requirements planning logistics and supply chain software
skills.def: Software to manage, monitor, or optimize the flow of goods or services from an origin point to a destination. Examples: Fleet management software.

skills.name: Mobile location based services software
skills.def: Software to provide content or services based on a device's geographical location. Examples: Global positioning system GPS software.

skills.name: Time accounting software
skills.def: Software to submit or manage time accounting for human resources. Examples: Payroll software.
